{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"Match a system inventory against CVE advisories; report only applicable CVE IDs.

Input: JSON with `system_profile` (product names + versions) and `advisories` (id, description, affected).

Output: exactly {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique supplied IDs (empty array if none). No other text.

PRODUCT MATCHING:
1. Lowercase; treat hyphens, underscores, spaces, and slashes as equivalent separators.
2. Strip vendor/organization prefixes when the advisory name is vendor/product ("jetbrains/teamcity" = "teamcity"; "m-files/m-files_server" = "m-files-server"). Also strip a vendor prefix that starts the installed name.
3. Match ONLY when the ENTIRE normalized product name agrees after vendor stripping ("apache/superset" = "apache-superset" = "superset"). Ignore case.
4. Descriptions may restate the product name differently (Title Case, package-manager hyphens) — use them to confirm matches when naming style differs.
5. Do NOT match different products sharing a vendor ("jetbrains-hub" ≠ "jetbrains/teamcity"; "sap-solution-manager" ≠ "sap/content_server"). Partial token overlap is NOT a match. If no installed product matches, the CVE is NOT applicable even if the vendor appears in the inventory.
6. Multi-branch advisories (OR-separated): applicable if ANY branch matches an installed product AND that branch's version condition holds.

VERSION COMPARISON (mechanical, numeric, segment-wise — never approximate):
1. Split on dots; compare segments AS INTEGERS left to right. Pad the shorter with zeros first: 3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1; 720.0 == 720; 20230607.0 == 20230607.
2. Integer segment comparison: 10 > 6; 100 > 45; 757.1 > 757; 4.12.9 < 4.12.56860; 5.10 > 5.6; 2024.2.1 > 2024.2; 19.15 > 19.14; 22.6.3.0 > 22.6.2; 9.0.18 > 9.0.17; 2024.10 > 2024.2; 19.15.1 > 19.15.
3. Operators: "=" equality after zero-padding; "<" strict; "<=" inclusive (installed == bound IS affected); ">=" inclusive. Range ">= A and < B" means A <= installed < B.
4. Prose: "prior to X", "before X", "up to but excluding X" → STRICT < X (installed == X is EXCLUDED). "up to and including X", "X and prior", "X and below" → inclusive <= X.
5. Date-like versions (20230913, 20230904) are ordinary versions; compare numerically with bounds exactly as stated.

DECISION PROCEDURE — for each advisory, do BOTH checks explicitly:
(a) PRODUCT: find installed products matching per rules 1-6. No match → skip (even if vendor or topic appears in inventory or description).
(b) VERSION: for each matched product, evaluate EVERY branch mechanically against the installed version.
   INCLUDE when the installed version satisfies a branch:
   - installed strictly BELOW a "<" bound: 9.0.17 < 9.0.18 → AFFECTED; 23.4.12528.2 < 23.11.13156.0 → AFFECTED; 2023.3.10 < 2023.3.3? NO (10 > 3). Compare each segment as an integer.
   - installed AT or BELOW a "<=" bound: 19.15 <= 19.15 → AFFECTED; 19.15.1 <= 19.15? NO.
   - installed AT or ABOVE a ">=" lower bound AND below any upper bound: 8.0.0.1 >= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.1 → AFFECTED.
   - installed EQUAL to an "=" bound after zero-padding: 1.0.0.0.0 == 1.0.0.0 → AFFECTED.
   EXCLUDE when the installed version is at or above an exclusive upper bound, below an inclusive lower bound, or fails an "=" bound:
   - 23.4.12528.2 vs "< 23.4.12528.1" → 2 > 1 → EXCLUDED.
   - 4.0.20.1 vs "< 4.0.20.0" → EXCLUDED; 10.9 vs "< 10.8" → 9 > 8 → EXCLUDED.
   - 8.31.0 vs "< 8.31.0" → equal → EXCLUDED; 5.10.0.1 vs "< 5.10.0" → equal after padding → EXCLUDED.
   - 2024.3.52635.0 vs "< 2024.3.52635" → equal after padding → EXCLUDED.
   - 2.2.14.1 vs "= 2.2.14" → NOT equal → EXCLUDED.
   - 3.7.10 vs ">= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2" → 10 > 2 → EXCLUDED; 9.4.2.1 vs "<= 9.4.2" → EXCLUDED.
   - 2024.10 vs "< 2024.2" → 10 > 2 → EXCLUDED (treat 2024.10 as version 2024.10, not a date).
   NEVER include on product name alone without a satisfied version branch. NEVER drop a CVE whose version branch IS satisfied — including when the installed version is only slightly below the bound (any version below a "<" bound is affected, no matter how small the gap), when inclusive bounds are exactly met, or when the installed version has extra trailing segments equal after zero-padding (1.0.0.0.0 == 1.0.0.0 → AFFECTED).
   Worked range example: 8.0.0.1 >= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.1 → 0 = 0, 0 < 11 → AFFECTED. 1.1.0.0 vs "= 1.0.0.0 OR = 1.1.0.0" → AFFECTED.
(c) Report each applicable ID once.

REMINDERS:
- Alias-style naming differences (vendor/slash, hyphens, underscores, Title Case) never justify dropping a CVE — normalize and match.
- Trailing zeros: X.Y.Z.0 == X.Y.Z; X.Y.Z.1 > X.Y.Z; X.Y.Z.0.0 == X.Y.Z.
- Check equality before exclusion: installed == strict bound → EXCLUDED; installed == inclusive bound → INCLUDED.
- Version segments are integers: compare 10 vs 2 numerically, never lexically or as dates.
- Evaluate each advisory independently; return only the JSON
